newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece drafts bill on new bourse emergency fund.
newsitem.headline: Greece drafts bill on new bourse emergency fund.

text.p: A draft bill that outlines the establishment of an emergency clearing fund at the Athens stock exchange, designed to step in and cover settlement defaults promptly, was submitted to parliament on Tuesday.
Coming on the heels of last year's Delta Securities scandal which closed down the exchange for four days, the fund will not be a legal entity but will be managed by the Athens stock exchange.

The bill, presented by the National Economy Ministry, calls for the creation of an "Athens Stock Exchange Auxiliary Clearing Fund" to solve liquidity bottlenecks at the clearing house when member brokers fail to settle either in cash or securities.
Based on the bill, the Athens bourse, the fund's manager and custodian, will activate it at its board's discretion.
When settlement failures at the clearing house upset the stock market, the fund will be available for some fast firefighting.
The bill specifies that future settlement failures must exceed a threshold of 5.0 percent of the bourse's average daily trading volume in the most recent semester for the emergency fund to step in.

Procedurally, the clearing house will inform the bourse daily on the amount of trades that are not being settled promptly. The fund may not use more than half of its assets without prior clearance by the capital markets commission.

When a member broker fails to settle promptly with the clearing house and the emergency fund steps in, the broker must meet a set three-month deadline to settle its financial obligations with the emergency fund.
If this is not met, the fund may in turn seek retribution from the exchange's guarantee fund.
The bill also states how the emergency fund's initial capital will be funded.
The bourse will contribute 0.02 percent of the exchange's total turnover in 1995 and 1996. Member brokers will also have to come up with 0.01 percent of their total trading volume in 1995 and 1996.

Last year trading volume at the Athens stock exchange reached 3.979 billion drachmas. The top 15 brokers shared 65 percent of the bourse's turnover leaving 35 percent for the other 49 exchange members. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
